at.piece: J. Strauss II, An der schoenen blauen Donau (Blue Danube), the opening horn theme
at.note: Track 1 single-note line: beats 0-6 (C C E G G-G, the horn call) then its repeat from beat 48-52 (C C E G C5, ending on high C5). Echo chords at E5/G5 omitted. Original key C (file), no transposition. Waltz 3/4, q is the quarter. The bar-3 gap kept as a one-beat rest. Not a fanfare strictly, but the tune is instantly recognisable and festive; Strauss II is Viennese.

be.piece: Matelotte (Walloon fiddle dance from the Ardennes), first part
be.source: https://trillian.mit.edu/~jc/music/abc/Belgium/Matelotte.abc and mirror/musicaviva.com/belgium/matelotte-180100.abc (from Jean Guillaume Houssa's fiddler's notebook, Soy-lez-Durbuy, c.1850; K:D, M:2/4, L:1/16), transcribed by hand
be.note: First part: pickup D F plus 8 bars, final d lengthened to 1.5 beats; no transposition (range 62-81). Beat = quarter (sixteenth 0.25). Real Belgian (Walloon) folk tune but not famous; the Flemish side is already covered by De Vlaamse Leeuw. Gossec/Franck/Vieuxtemps scores or MIDI not found in the allowed sources.

bg.source: https://trillian.mit.edu/~jc/music/abc/Bulgaria/RACH1.abc (J. Chambers, X:1 in G, 7/8, L:1/8, part B)
bg.note: Bars 1-3 + 1st ending (c B A B G A B), repeated with the 2nd ending G2 G D G; final G lengthened to 2 beats (written G + rest). Ornament marks (~) omitted; F# per K:G. Range 62-76.

ca.piece: Vive la Canadienne (French-Canadian fiddle setting, second half of the A part, bars 5-11)
ca.source: abcnotation.com tune page for tunearch.org/wiki/Vive_la_canadienne_(1) (transcribed by Andrew Kuntz from Isidore Soucy's 1927 recording, Starr 15312-B), abc K:G L:1/8 M:C, bars 5-10 plus the 2nd ending
ca.note: UNCERTAIN: a fiddle setting, not checked against a sung score (tunearch.org blocks scripted access). No Canadian classical composer with an accessible PD score was found (Lavallee wrote the anthem; Maple Leaf Forever is politically loaded in Quebec). Verify by ear; drop the country if it is not recognisable. Ends on G held. Unit: quarter = 1 beat.

cz.piece: Fucik, Vjezd gladiatoru (Entry of the Gladiators, Op. 68), the chromatic run and main theme
cz.note: Top line of beats 42.5-56 in the file: chromatic run C5..B5 (0.5 beat each), then C6 B5 A#5 B5 A#5 A5 G#5 G5 F#5 G5. Ends on G5 (fifth) held over a C major chord because the phrase continues in the score. File is in C, no transposition; peaks at C6 = MIDI 84. Fucik died 1916; Czech composer.

de.piece: Mendelssohn, Wedding March (A Midsummer Night's Dream, Op. 61), the opening trumpet fanfare
de.note: Beats 3-20 of the file (bars 1-5): triplet C4 fanfare x3, then E4, then G4 (top line of tracks 1/2). Ends on G4 (fifth of the tonic chord) held under the C major chord, since the score goes straight on into the theme; original key C major, no transposition. First 3 beats of rest dropped.

dk.piece: Marken er mejet (Danish harvest song), melody
dk.source: https://trillian.mit.edu/~jc/music/abc/mirror/musicaviva.com/denmark/marken-er-mejet.abc (Musica Viva abc, K:A, M:2/4, L:1/8), transcribed by hand
dk.note: First 8 bars (the A part, 'A4' final bar) as written; no transposition (range 69-81); last A lengthened to 2.5 beats; beat = quarter. Lumbye (Champagne Galop) would be the classical choice but no MIDI/abc/score was reachable in the allowed sources (IMSLP PDF download not attempted), so folk.

fi.piece: Alkumarssi (opening march), Haapavesi fiddle tune, A part with second ending
fi.source: https://trillian.mit.edu/~jc/music/abc/Finland/march/Alkumarssi_D.abc (John Chambers, from 'Haapaveden purpurista', Kesajuhlat 2013 Saarijarvi; K:D, M:C, L:1/8), transcribed by hand
fi.note: First part: bars 1-3 of the first ending then the second-ending bar 'e2Bc d2d2', last d lengthened to 2 beats. No transposition (range 69-81). Beat = quarter (eighth 0.5). Not a famous tune: a genuine Finnish folk march from a fiddlers' collection, since classical options (Sibelius d.1957) are still in copyright and Karjalan/Ievan polkka scores are uncertain or arranged by 20th-century composers. Skip this if recognisability matters more.

gb.piece: Rule, Britannia! (Arne), the chorus line 'Rule, Britannia, Britannia rule the waves'
gb.source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Rule,_Britannia_(pg).mid (Wikimedia Commons MIDI, 'pg'), vocal-line track parsed with parse_midi.py; beats 32.0-38.5 of that track (G major)
gb.note: Chorus first line from its pickup A to the long G; no transposition (range 67-74); last note lengthened to 1.5 beats; rhythms rounded to eighth/sixteenth. Elgar / Clarke / Purcell not found as MIDI or score in the allowed sources (Mutopia has none), so Arne's tune; mildly patriotic but not disputed. Alternative if unwanted: skip.

gr.note: First strain bars 1-3 + 1st ending, repeated, then 2nd ending G2 D G2; final G lengthened to 2 beats (the written rest dropped). Grace notes omitted; F is F# (K:G). No transposition (range 67-79).

hr.piece: Drmeš iz Zdenčine (Croatian drmeš dance), first strain
hr.source: https://trillian.mit.edu/~jc/music/abc/Croatia/DrmesIzZdencine.abc (J. Chambers, X:2 in D, M:C| L:1/8; top note of each written chord)
hr.note: Pickup F# + 4 bars of strain A, ending on the D tonic (3 eighths). Top note of chords only. No transposition (range 74-81).

ie.source: https://trillian.mit.edu/~jc/music/abc/Ireland/jig/Irish_Washerwoman-JC-G-32-2.abc (John Chambers, K:G, M:6/8, L:1/8), transcribed by hand
ie.note: First (A) strain: pickup d/c/ then 8 bars; bar 8 'BGG G2' ends with the final G held. Beat = quarter note (eighth = 0.5). No transposition (range 62-76).

is.piece: Ríðum, ríðum (Icelandic children's riding song), melody
is.source: https://trillian.mit.edu/~jc/music/abc/mirror/musicaviva.com/iceland/ridum-ridum.abc (Musica Viva abc transcribed by Frank Nordberg, K:Em, M:C, L:1/4), transcribed by hand
is.note: A part (4 bars) then B part with its second ending (G F# E2 -> final E held 3 beats); transposed up one octave (original range 64-72, here 76-84); beat = quarter. Only the abc source's title/origin vouches that this is the Icelandic song; uncertain, so skip if you want only famous tunes. No Icelandic classical piece found.

no.piece: Grieg, Wedding Day at Troldhaugen (Lyric Pieces Op. 65 no. 6), opening theme
no.note: Right hand from the pickup triplet in bar 2 (beat 7.5 of the file, A major) to the first cadence note A at beat 22; the opening repeated-A fanfare bars skipped; last note lengthened to 1.5 beats; no transposition (range 66-78).

pl.piece: Chopin, Polonaise in A-flat major, Op. 53 ('Heroic'), first theme (bars 17-24)
pl.source: piano-midi.de (Bernd Krueger, CC BY-SA 3.0 DE) chpn_op53.mid via web.archive.org/web/2020id_/http://www.piano-midi.de/midis/chopin/chpn_op53.mid, parsed with parse_midi.py
pl.note: Top line (right hand, a line in thirds; upper voice taken) of beats 48-56 of the file, i.e. the theme right after the 16-bar introduction. Written enharmonically in the file (D#=Eb). Key A-flat major, no transposition. Ends on Eb5 held over an A-flat chord. A few ornamental 32nd notes in bar 55 smoothed (a 0.125 gap kept). The identification of these bars as THE famous first theme rests on position (bar 17 after the intro), not on a second source: moderate confidence.

ro.source: trillian.mit.edu/~jc/music/abc/Romania/Ciocarlanul_C.abc (J. Chambers, from a handwritten MS), second part, K:C L:1/8 M:4/4
ro.note: Four bars, the 2nd strain of the abc (Am), ending on A held. No Romanian classical piece with an accessible PD score was found (Ivanovici's Waves of the Danube and Enescu are on IMSLP only, which blocks scripted downloads; Commons has just a cover). Range 68-77 (G# is the harmonic-minor leading tone).

rs.source: https://trillian.mit.edu/~jc/music/abc/Serbia/ShumadiskoKolo.abc (J. Chambers, X:1, K:G, L:1/16, first strain A)
rs.note: Strain A: groups 1-3 + 1st ending, repeated, 2nd pass ends with the 1st ending again, last G (written as a sixteenth) lengthened to 2 beats so it ends on the tonic instead of the written B. Range 62-79.

ru.piece: March of the Wooden Soldiers (Album for the Young, Op. 39 No. 5), opening 8 bars
ru.source: Mutopia Project https://www.mutopiaproject.org/ftp/TchaikovskyPI/O39/05MarchOfTheWoodenSoldiers/05MarchOfTheWoodenSoldiers.mid, track 1 top line, beats 0-16 (D major)
ru.note: Notes are played legato at the written lengths (the MIDI has them detached; repeated D's are re-articulated). Final D (the 16th beat) held, no transposition. Range 70-79.

se.piece: Ack Värmeland, du sköna (Swedish folk song), first half
se.source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ack_Värmeland,_du_sköna.mid (Commons MIDI, melody track parsed with parse_midi.py); first note A3 to the first long D, ending of the first half
se.note: Beats 0.5-27.5 of the melody track (D minor with raised 7th C#); no transposition (range 57-76; only the opening pickup A3=57 sits below 60); last D lengthened to 2.5 beats; a 0.5-beat breath rest kept after bar 4; rhythm rounded to quarter/eighth. Stately rather than fanfare-like, but a lively well-known Värmland tune.

tr.piece: Harmandali (Aegean zeybek/harmandali dance tune), opening phrase twice
tr.source: trillian.mit.edu/~jc/music/abc/mirror/SeymourShlien/makams/makamu9.abc, X:968 (from CompMusic/SymbTr, compmusic.upf.edu/node/140), K:C with B flat, F#, C#; L:1/16 M:9/4
tr.note: First two lines of the abc: the 9/4 phrase, the 2nd time an octave higher, ending on A (hicaz, tonic A) held. The comma-microtones of the source key signature are rounded to 12-TET; the phrase itself uses only D E F# G A. Chord is an open fifth A-E. Uncertain only in tempo/feel (zeybek is usually slower).

ua.note: Part A: bars 1-4, 1-2, 7 and the closing D. Bar 4 is 'a4' then the chord [d' a f]; the melody takes a (81) and the top d' (86, above the usual range). Last bar shortened to D held (the abc has 'd2 z2 [chord]'). G# persists inside a bar per abc rules (as notated). Hutsul/Ukrainian dance, widely known.

us.piece: The Stars and Stripes Forever, introduction (bars 1-8)
us.source: Mutopia Project https://www.mutopiaproject.org/ftp/SousaJP/TheStarsAndStripesForever/TheStarsAndStripesForever.mid (piano score, Cincinnati: John Church Co., 1897; key Eb, 2/2), top line of the right hand, beats 0-16 of the MIDI
us.note: The right hand is doubled in octaves; the upper octave is used (Eb5..Bb5). Eb D Eb C Eb, then the chromatic climb F F# G Ab A Bb, a rest, and the closing Bb held. The intro ends on Bb (the dominant of Eb), so the held chord is the Eb tonic chord under it (Bb is its fifth). Beats are quarter notes of the 2/2 bar at q 0.25 (the file's tempo is 0.25 s per beat).
